attack_b.turn_convention: One turn = one assistant message. A message may bundle several slot questions (this is the convention the shipped harness already uses: `minimal_questions` returns a LIST of questions and the simulated oracle answers every asked slot inside that one message). The dialogue ends when the partial rule is complete (`_partial_complete`) or the policy returns no question. `turns` = number of assistant messages; `slots_asked` = number of slot questions asked across the dialogue (reported separately because a bundled question costs one turn but one slot). The protocol is fixed across all variants and identical to the shipped harness (seed 0xC3A1, reps=3, k=rep+1 masked slots of {event, zone, threshold}).
attack_b.selection_rule: Pre-registered on the DEV split only: maximise rule-correctness; tie-break on the lower mean number of turns; final tie-break on the lower mean number of slot questions. The winner is frozen and evaluated ONCE on the TEST split.

+def _combine_bounds(bounds: List[Dict[str, Any]], unit: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Combine conjunctive bounds of one unit family into a single threshold.
+
+    A request may state several bounds of the same unit ("more than five but
+    fewer than ten people").  Keeping only one of them silently widens the
+    rule: the created alert then fires in configurations the user excluded.
+    This helper returns the conjunction of ``bounds`` as one threshold
+    (``between`` for a two-sided range, the strictest bound otherwise) and
+    ``None`` when the bounds cannot be combined.
+    """
+    lowers = [b for b in bounds if b["op"] in {">", ">="}]
+    uppers = [b for b in bounds if b["op"] in {"<", "<="}]
+    exact = [b for b in bounds if b["op"] == "=="]
